site: Royals Auction Arena - Pressure Lab (historical performance under pressure; not a retention or auction-buy recommendation)

batting.source: Final 18 November 2026 historical pressure analysis of 843 completed matches from the competition-supplied match list (2022-2026). Ball-by-ball records were recovered for those fixtures.
method: Pressure before the ball

The pressure score combines leverage (30%), collapse risk (25%), required-rate stress (25%) and match balance (20%), all measured from information available before the ball. The weights are a declared starting choice.
One shared pressure set

A delivery is high pressure when its pre-ball score reaches 0.507: the top 35% of all 199,211 deliveries, 69,724 balls (35,922 first innings, 33,802 second innings) on one common scale. Every player is measured over the same fixed set of high-pressure states from all 843 matches.
Expected-performance models

Three model families estimate the expected ball outcome, the run value of a position and changes in win probability. The 843 matches are split into fixed groups; each match is evaluated using models trained on the other groups. Run expectancy values a wicket by the runs the batting side would still be expected to score. Win probability is one smooth model calibrated on held-out matches.
Batting: value above expectation

A is wicket-aware adjusted run value: runs scored plus the change in expected remaining team runs, compared with what an average batter was expected to produce in the same situations and bowling contexts. High-pressure A sets the batting rank.
Recency and partial pooling

Player estimates use a 365-day half-life recency weighting chosen in advance. Partial pooling combines individual evidence with the population pattern, so players with fewer pressure balls get a more balanced estimate.
The 0-100 score
Score = 100 x Phi(z), where z compares estimated A with the role average in population standard deviations. 50 is the role average. Batting and bowling use separate scales.
Selection

Every identity in the modelled pool (838 batters, 572 bowlers) is scored. The final lists cover the 14 batters and 16 bowlers with substantial high-pressure evidence; the report presents the top 10 of each.
batting.caveat: The final list ranks performance under pressure itself, based on 843 completed matches from 2022-2026. The 80% score intervals are conditional and wide (about 77 points for top-10 batters and 75 for top-10 bowlers), so treat close ranks as approximate; they omit model-form and calibration uncertainty.
